 Fulham in form published at 11:44 GMT 11:44 GMT 
 Man City v Fulham (12:30 GMT) 
 Worth pointing out that unlike Manchester City, Fulham are a team in form.
 The visitors are unbeaten in their past four Premier League games (W2, D2), and have lost just one of their past seven (W2 D4). 
 There have been as many goals in their previous seven games (11 – F6, A5) as in their opening three fixtures of the campaign (F4, A7).
 4 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'I don't think they were the worst team' published at 11:41 GMT 11:41 GMT 
 Man City v Fulham (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa is not reading too much into Manchester City's recent poor form.
 After failing to win their first seven Premier League games, Fulham are unbeaten in their last four, winning two of them.
 Speaking about City's three-game losing run, Arbeloa said: "The last three games that they lost I didn't think they were the worst team, so they have the chances. 
 "You can see the quality of the players and how they want to play. They are very aggressive when they lose the ball and they are performing really well."
 2 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Perfect opponent for City? published at 11:37 GMT 11:37 GMT 
 Man City v Fulham (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Manchester City have lost their last three Premier League games in a row, but their past form against Fulham will give them confidence of ending that run today.
 City have won the last 20 encounters between the two sides, and boss Enzo Maresca said: "Hopefully 21! It's a long time. Hopefully we can continue winning games against them."
 On City's form, he added: "I was not thinking we were doing everything well when we were winning games. I'm not thinking we did everything wrong when we lost games. There are things we need to do better and no doubt we will do better."
 7 9 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'I'm expecting Man City to be much better' published at 11:34 GMT 11:34 GMT 
 Man City v Fulham (12:30 GMT) 
 The wheels have come off for Enzo Maresca at Manchester City with three Premier League defeats in a row.
 It's not just City's results which have been alarming, either - they were well beaten by Nottingham Forest last time out, and their performance would have been the biggest concern for their manager.
 In contrast, Fulham 's results have improved of late and they are unbeaten in four league games. They've done all right whenever I've seen them this season, so I'm not surprised to see them picking up points.
 Still, the international break probably came at a good time for Maresca to sort things out. Erling Haaland is scoring again too - not that he ever really stopped for very long - and I'm expecting City to be much better here.
 I'm even going for them to keep a clean sheet, for the first time in eight games. I'm always brave... which is why I am bottom of the predictions table.
 Sutton's prediction: 2-0

 Post published at 11:27 GMT 11:27 GMT 
 Man City v Fulham (12:30 GMT) 
 Just discovered a brutal stat.
 Manchester City have won their past 17 Premier League games against Fulham, scoring at least twice each time. It’s the longest winning streak one team has had against another in English league history. 
 Gosh, the longest ever. I reckon we can turn this into a Get Involved. Who are your club's bogey team? The opponent where no matter what, no matter the league position, your side always seem to lose to.

 Team news published at 11:19 GMT 11:19 GMT 
 Man City v Fulham (12:30 GMT) 
 Abdukodir Khusanov is passed fit for Manchester City, while
Marc Guehi also starts after missing the England games through injury. Enzo
Fernandez and Rayan Cherki are both benched.
 City make three changes from the side who lost to Nottingham
Forest before the international break with Nico O’Reilly, Ayyoub Bouaddi and
Phil Foden replacing Josko Gvardiol, Fernand
 Man City XI: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gurhi, O'Reilly, Anderson, Bouaddi, Foden, Ndiaye, Doku, Haaland. Subs: Rulli, Kovacic, Cherki, Fernandez, Reis, Gvardiol, Allan, Samba, Lewis.
 Fulham also make three changes from their 1-1 draw with Newcastle
earlier this month. Kenny Tete, Ryan Sessegnon and Rodrigo Muniz come in for
Timothy Castagne, Antonee Robinson and Gonzalo Garcia.
 Fulham XI: Leno, Tete, Bassey, Affengruber, Sessegnon, Charles, Berge, King, Muniz, Iwobi, Bobb. Subs: Kaiser, Cuenca, García, Palacios, Cairney, Larsson, Angel, Castagne, Robinson.
